turns_text: [SEG0001] person_1 (NURSE): Come through, the corridor is very noisy today, sorry about the wait.
[SEG0002] person_2 (PATIENT): Ya, I can't hear myself think out there. And now I've got a frog in my throat, just nerves, it's nothing.
[SEG0003] person_1 (NURSE): Shoes off please, we'll do the weight and the pressure.
[SEG0004] person_2 (PATIENT): Weight will be up only. I've overdone it with the laddoos at home, that's all, not a big problem.
[SEG0005] person_1 (NURSE): Today you are 74.5 kilograms, height 158 centimetres. The file says 68 from last year, I'm not using that figure.
[SEG0006] person_2 (PATIENT): See, sweets. It's fine, don't look so serious.
[SEG0007] person_1 (NURSE): Blood pressure is 122 over 78, pulse 84. Doctor will see you now.
[SEG0008] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'm Dr. Mehta. Your mother fixed the visit, but what is actually bothering you?
[SEG0009] person_2 (PATIENT): Nothing much. Pimples on the face, and the periods are a bit off. She fussed, I didn't want to come.
[SEG0010] person_3 (DOCTOR): How are the periods off, exactly?
[SEG0011] person_2 (PATIENT): They come every two months, sometimes three. Since two years. Normal for me only, I don't care.
[SEG0012] person_3 (DOCTOR): And the spots, how long now?
[SEG0013] person_2 (PATIENT): From first year college, so three years. Cheeks and chin. Just spots, I'm not crying over them.
[SEG0014] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any coarse hair on the chin or the upper lip?
[SEG0015] person_2 (PATIENT): A little on the chin. I thread it. Every girl has some, why the fuss?
[SEG0016] person_3 (DOCTOR): The weight, over how long has it climbed?
[SEG0017] person_2 (PATIENT): I can't say when it started. Sometime in college. Clothes are tight, so what. I've overdone the eating, finished.
[SEG0018] person_3 (DOCTOR): Energy wise, any other feeling in the body?
[SEG0019] person_2 (PATIENT): By evening I feel like a wet rag. And if I stand too long in the lab my feet feel dead. Ignore both, everyone gets that.
[SEG0020] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me think aloud. Spots, late cycles, chin hair, weight up. This can be a polycystic ovary pattern, but I am not confirming it sitting here.
[SEG0021] person_2 (PATIENT): Don't make pimples into a disease, doctor.
[SEG0022] person_3 (DOCTOR): The ovary can put out a little extra male-type hormone, so acne, hair and irregular menses travel as a set. Tests decide it, not my guess.
[SEG0023] person_2 (PATIENT): If you say so. From my side it's still nothing.
[SEG0024] person_3 (DOCTOR): When the period does come, is the bleeding heavy, clots, soaking through pads?
[SEG0025] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Late, that's all. Not heavy.
[SEG0026] person_3 (DOCTOR): What about thirst, or passing urine much more than before?
[SEG0027] person_2 (PATIENT): Mm, I suppose. Sometimes, not really.
[SEG0028] person_3 (DOCTOR): I'll leave that fuzzy. On the tummy side, loose motions, constipation, pain as a regular thing?
[SEG0029] person_2 (PATIENT): Tummy is fine. Nothing like that.
[SEG0030] person_3 (DOCTOR): Do you yourself have diabetes, or a thyroid problem?
[SEG0031] person_2 (PATIENT): No. Only my mother has sugar, tablets for many years. I'm healthy.
[SEG0032] person_3 (DOCTOR): Her diabetes still counts. With this weight I can't rule out an early sugar issue in you, even if you feel well. That sits separate from the ovary thought.
[SEG0033] person_2 (PATIENT): She takes the medicine. I don't. Please, no tablets for me.
[SEG0034] person_3 (DOCTOR): Any tablets or creams just now?
[SEG0035] person_2 (PATIENT): Umm, adapaline gel last year, for two months, then I left it. Face was peeling. Nothing now.
[SEG0036] person_3 (DOCTOR): Right, so that gel is stopped, and I am not starting any hormone pill today.
[SEG0037] person_2 (PATIENT): My friend eats some pill for her skin. I don't want that.
[SEG0038] person_3 (DOCTOR): A combined pill, drospirenone with ethinylestradiol, can settle cycles and help acne. If these reports fit, we might start it at the next visit. Not now.
[SEG0039] person_2 (PATIENT): We'll see. Maybe never.
[SEG0040] person_3 (DOCTOR): Let me look. Inflamed spots and blackheads on the cheeks and chin, and a few coarse hairs along the chin. May I check the abdomen?
[SEG0041] person_2 (PATIENT): Go ahead. You won't find anything.

[SEG0042] person_3 (DOCTOR): Abdomen is soft, no mass. So my working impression is possible polycystic ovary syndrome, and I still can't exclude a glucose problem with the gain and your mother's sugar.
[SEG0043] person_2 (PATIENT): Possible only. Don't write it in big letters on the file.

[SEG0044] person_3 (DOCTOR): For this ovary pattern, and to check the sugar side, I'll book fasting bloods, glucose, HbA1c, TSH, testosterone, LH and FSH, plus a pelvic ultrasound. Both are arranged, not a maybe.
[SEG0045] person_2 (PATIENT): Needles and a scan for pimples. If you insist.
[SEG0046] person_1 (NURSE): Fasting blood form is with you, and the scan is Thursday at eight in the morning. Come empty stomach, bloods that same morning. The slot is already booked.
[SEG0047] person_2 (PATIENT): Thursday I have a practical. Does it have to be then?
[SEG0048] person_1 (NURSE): Kindly come Thursday itself, the test is fixed. If you are a little late we will still take you.
[SEG0049] person_3 (DOCTOR): Cut back the laddoos, steady only, not a crash diet. That part sits with you.
[SEG0050] person_2 (PATIENT): I'll try. No promises. The canteen is right there.
[SEG0051] person_3 (DOCTOR): Come back in three weeks with both reports, and we decide about the pill then. If you feel badly unwell before that, call us, don't sit on it.
[SEG0052] person_2 (PATIENT): Three weeks. My class is starting, I can go, no?

spec.situation: Young woman with acne and irregular periods for two years, some facial hair, weight gain; mother had diabetes; bloods and pelvic scan planned; contraceptive pill discussed, not started.

traps.happens: The patient describes things in colourful or sentence-like speech ('I've overdone it', 'I can't hear myself think', 'a frog in my throat', 'my feet feel dead', 'I feel like a wet rag').
traps.label_rule: Every symptom name is a short clinical noun phrase of 1 to 5 words ('voice fatigue', 'numbness in both feet', 'tiredness'), never a full sentence, never starting with I/we/my. Pure idioms that are not symptoms ('I can't hear myself think' said about classroom noise) are NOT symptoms. The patient's own words stay in the cited turn, not in the name.

features: ambiguous_answer: an answer that sounds like yes but is really 'maybe' ('mm, I suppose', 'sometimes, not really'); recorded with uncertainty or not at all, never as a firm fact.
doctor_misses_topics: the doctor does not ask about everything; topics never discussed are simply absent (no invented denials, no allergy line if allergies were never mentioned).

bad.reason: Tests and Thursday timing supported; 8 a.m. explicitly stated for scan, not clearly bloods.
bad.text: Fasting blood tests for glucose, HbA1c, TSH, testosterone, LH and FSH (action_type=investigation, status=planned, responsible_person=doctor, time_reference=value: Thursday at 8 in the morning)

omissions.text: Patient denied soaking through pads and denied clots with menses; only late periods were reported.
Thirst/polyuria symptoms were asked about but response was equivocal/uncertain ('sometimes, not really'); this uncertainty was not recorded.
Current medication status was explicitly 'nothing now' after stopping adapalene gel.
Adapalene gel caused facial peeling, which was the reason it was stopped.
Doctor explicitly stated he was not starting any hormone pill today.
Abdominal examination also found the abdomen was soft.
Nurse instructed the patient to come fasting/empty stomach for the blood tests and scan the same morning.
